title: Azure subscription detail
description: Reads a subscription's name and state; requires owner-level rights, so most service principals cannot call it.

outputs.name: state
outputs.description: Enabled, Disabled, Deleted, PastDue or Warned

notes: subscription_id is required - this reads one subscription rather than enumerating them, so it cannot be used to discover which subscriptions a credential can reach. A service principal without the Owner role gets HTTP 401 with code UserNotAuthorized and the message that only subscription owners can perform the operation; that is the expected result for the least-privilege credentials most automation uses, not a defect. When the goal is simply to confirm a credential works against a subscription, list resource groups instead - see azure/resource/resource-groups-lifecycle - which needs only Reader. This entry is draft because the owner-only path has not been exercised successfully; the authorization failure is the only behaviour that has been observed.
